Welcome to Glebe Primary School
We are delighted to welcome you to our Glebe website.
Your can also follow us on INSTAGRAM and TWITTER/X @gloriousglebe
WHAT IS SPECIAL ABOUT GLEBE?
Joining Glebe is joining a beautifully diverse community where every adult is ambitious for their child to be the best they can be! Our broad, ambitious curriculum inspires, engages and challenges our pupils and our ‘Rights Respecting’ ethos permeates throughout the school community. We have a strong focus on pastoral care and enrichment and believe in the importance of developing our pupils as well-rounded, happy individuals whose individual talents and interests are nurtured and enabled to grow. Our children take pride in their school and are actively involved in planning how we continue to evolve as a school.

Aims

inspire enthusiasm for learning and achieving,

Values and Beliefs
We are an inclusive ‘Rights Respecting School’ where children, parents/carers, staff, governors, and local services work in partnership to meet the needs of the community. We celebrate the positive contribution made by different social, ethnic and linguistic groups.
We have agreed a set of school values which we would like everyone in the school community to develop and follow:
Commitment: All members of the community demonstrating commitment to learning and achieving their own personal best.
Communication: All members of the community communicating clearly, confidently and with warmth and positivity.
Care: All members of the community treating ourselves, each other, visitors and our environment with kindness, consideration and compassion.

Welcome To Glebe
"Making a Positive Difference Together"
Our school aims are to:
These aims, along with our values of Commitment, Communication and Care, underpin the direction of the school and all the work that we do.

Schools Counselling Partnership
SCHOOLS COUNSELLING PARTNERSHIP AT GLEBE PRIMARY SCHOOL
Lucy Cohen is the Therapeutic Lead for the Counselling service (SCP) here at Glebe Primary School. Lucy has experience working as a child counsellor in Primary and Secondary schools across London. Lucy's passion is promoting the emotional wellbeing of children and young people, their families and school staff and SCP offer a wraparound service to meet these needs.
You will find Lucy at Glebe Primary School on Tuesday
WHAT DO SCP OFFER AS A SERVICE?
Supporting Parents -
There are times when we could all do with someone to talk to, parents included. If you would like to meet with Lucy for a safe and confidential chat about you, your child or any concerns you might have. Lucy is available to meet with you every Tuesday 9am-10am
Supporting Children -
Lucy offers a lunchtime drop-in for children who want to talk about any feelings or worries they may have: your child knows this as 'The Space'.

Music
At Glebe Primary School we provide opportunities for all pupils to create, play, perform and enjoy music. We want every pupil to experience a wide variety of musical forms and appreciate the importance of making music together.
Article 28 – Every child has the right to a good quality education.
Article 29 – Education should help children to develop their talents and abilities.

Link Governor
Reviewed as part of the Circle Model of Governance
Progression Document
music progression document.pdf
Intent, Implementation and Impact
Curriculum Intent
At Glebe Primary School, our music curriculum intends to deliver a high-quality music education which engages and inspires all pupils to develop a love of music, to identify and nurture their talent as musicians, and so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement.
Curriculum Implementation
At Glebe we use the Music’s Cool syllabus across both Key stages. We have a range of instrumental tuition delivered by peripatetic staff from the Harrow Music Service. We currently offer tuition on the flute, clarinet, keyboard, guitar, violin, tabla, harmonium, recorder, drumkit and steel pans. Children are taught in small groups of four for 30 mins each week. Children are taught class music once a week as part of the curriculum for 40 or 50 minutes.
We aim to implement the intent by giving the children opportunity to
Curriculum Impact
A rounded musical experience for every child, giving them opportunities to develop vocal, listening, instrumental and performance skills. Every year children who learn an instrument through small group teaching have the opportunity to participate in the Harrow Music Service music festivals alongside children from other schools in the borough. These are the Band, Guitar, String, World Music, Recorder and Song Festivals. Once a year, either at Christmas or in the summer, staff from the Harrow Music Service come to Glebe to perform for the children. Over the years the Junior School Choir have had many opportunities to perform in different venues including the Camden Round House and the Royal Albert Hall with the BBC Singers. They have also performed in more local venues such Care homes and outside supermarkets such as Sainsburys. The school Band have attended the Bright Sparks concerts by the London Philharmonic Orchestra for KS2 at the Royal Festival Hall for many consecutive years. The children have regular opportunities to perform to audiences in school throughout the year in class assemblies and for Diwali, Christmas, the Infant and Junior Spring concerts, the PTFA Summer Fair and the Year 6 end of year production
Opportunities for performance develop self – confidence which can be readily noticed when the end result following weeks of practice and rehearsal is compared with the standard of playing or singing at the outset. We know the impact of collaborative learning and enjoyment in creative learning have been achieved when the children are eager to demonstrate their group learning ideas with confidence, in performance to rest of the class. We know also that the impact of regular singing has an immense effect on morale and well – being. This is evident when the children are still singing cheerfully in the corridor having left the hall or Music Room.
Instrumental Tuition
Across the school around 170 pupils are currently learning a musical instrument. Pupils are able to choose from keyboard, violin, guitar, flute, clarinet, recorder, tabla, harmonium, sitar and steel pans.
Glebe's Music Development Plan
We have developed our plan for the delivery of music through a child's time at Glebe:
gps music development plan.pdf
Concerts, Festivals and Productions
The special festivals of Diwali and Christmas are celebrated with productions by the Infants and Juniors. Every Spring term we have a Spring Concert which celebrates the musical skills and achievements of our pupils. Pupils learning instruments participate in Music Festivals throughout the year. In Year 6 pupils put on a production at the end of the Year to celebrate their time at Glebe.

Prospective Parents/Carers
On behalf of the staff, governors and children, I would like to welcome you to Glebe Primary School.
We are a learning community that truly believes in lifelong learning and the importance of strong partnerships with families to provide the best possible educational experiences and outcomes for our children.
Our children enjoy coming to school and are enthusiastic about learning.
We nurture and encourage curiosity and inspire children to be active participants in their own personal development and education. We provide a broad and balanced curriculum with a wide range of exciting enrichment opportunities such as special focus days and weeks, visits and visitors and extracurricular clubs.
Through lively and engaging teaching and learning, we nurture individual talents and provide challenge and support to ensure all children achieve their own personal best, again and again.
Glebe has a fantastic learning environment with vibrant classrooms and high-quality, well-resourced specialist areas which engage pupils in stimulating and meaningful activities to promote their well-being, learning and development across the curriculum. We have dedicated art, DT, food technology and music rooms where pupils enjoy exploring a range of media and techniques to further develop their creative skills. A visit to our study centre enables children to access excellent computing facilities or browse through our extensive selection of fiction and non-fiction books.
Our children enjoy learning outside and make good use of our field and school garden.
We strongly believe in the importance of capturing the pure joy that we see in our youngest children as they master basic skills or learn new facts and concepts for the first time and developing a thirst for learning throughout their time with us.
Our motto is ‘making a positive difference together’ and we are firmly committed to working closely with families and the wider community to ensure that we make a positive difference in all areas of school life.
We are thrilled that you are considering sending your child to Glebe. If you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact the school office. We will be very pleased to help!
We offer a MONDAY Prospective Parent/Carer tour. Go this this page for further details

If you would like to apply for a school place at Glebe Primary School you need to contact Harrow Council’s Admissions Department at Harrow Civic Centre. Staff in the school office do not manage admissions.
To apply for Nursery place and find out about nursery admission please visit https://www.harrow.gov.uk/schoolnursery
To apply for Primary school place and find out about primary school admission please visit www.harrow.gov.uk/schooladmissions

The Kenton Learning Centre (KLC)
Glebe Primary School shares its site with the Kenton Learning Centre (KLC). The centre is a well-resourced and attractive venue for adult and community learning. The provision at the KLC is organised and run through a partnership between Learn Harrow, Harrow Council’s adult learning team, and Glebe Primary School.
Adult learners, including the parents of the children at the school, have opportunities to access services and attend a range of learning activities including classes in computing, ESOL, first aid, family learning and basic skills. Some sessions are supported by crèche services.
Further information about the provision at the KLC can be obtained by:
Telephone on: 020 8204 3567
Email: learnharrow@harrow.gov.uk

The Mental Health Support Teams are an early intervention service who work in partnership with local schools to offer a whole school approach to mental health and wellbeing.They work with primary and secondary schools and colleges, in the boroughs of Brent, Harrow, and Hillingdon, delivering evidence-based interventions to support young people with mild to moderate mental health difficulties.

Ofsted and School Performance
CELEBRATING GLORIOUS GLEBE – OUR OFSTED REPORT 2026
We are delighted to share Glebe Primary School’s latest Ofsted report with you.
Following the inspection in the last week of the academic year in July 2026, Glebe has achieved the Expected Standard in every area inspected, with safeguarding standards also met.
For us, however, this report is about much more than a set of inspection outcomes. It tells the story of how far Glebe has come over the last two years and, most importantly, what it now feels like to be a child at our school.
What does the report say about Glebe?
Perhaps the part of the report that means the most to us is what inspectors heard from our children:
Our children told inspectors that the school “is much better now” and spoke warmly about being part of what they call “Glorious Glebe.” That matters.
To our staff, thank you for embracing change, continually improving your practice and caring so deeply about our children.
To our governors, thank you for the considerable time you give voluntarily and for providing both challenge and support as the school has improved.
To our parents and carers, thank you for trusting us, challenging us when needed, working alongside us and supporting the changes we have made. OFSTED’s recognition of the relationships between school and families is something we should all celebrate.
And, above all, to our children: thank you. Your positivity, character, diversity and ambition are what make Glebe glorious.
And now we go again We should celebrate how far we have come, but we are not complacent. Ofsted has identified the things we need to strengthen further, including outcomes for disadvantaged pupils, continuing to develop our wider curriculum and making sure adaptations for children with SEND and other barriers to learning are consistently effective. This links to our School Development Plan and the role the school, the children and you will play.
Our ambition is for Glebe to become even stronger. The difference now is that we know much more clearly what makes a successful Glebe: high expectations, strong teaching, excellent behaviour, genuine inclusion, committed staff, effective governance and a community that works together around its children.
Join the Glorious Glebe family!
For the full report, click here from 10th October 2026: https://reports.ofsted.gov.uk/provider/21/102224
